correctness.rationale: PASS. For the centered prism with n even>=6, generic plane-section vertices correspond bijectively to crossed prism edges, so the maximum of n+2 is the number of facets. On a fundamental azimuth sector 0<theta<beta=pi/n, opposite base-vertex projection pairs have two largest distinct magnitudes t1=cos theta and t2=cos(2beta-theta). With lambda=h|z|/sqrt(1-z²), all n lateral edges except the two pairs of projected largest vertices and four horizontal cap edges are crossed exactly when t2<lambda<t1; that event produces n+2 vertices. Uniform Haar azimuth and uniform |z| in [0,1], with P(lambda<t)=t/sqrt(h²+t²), integrate to p_n(h)=(n/pi)[2asin(sin beta/sqrt(1+h²))-asin(sin 2beta/sqrt(1+h²))]. For H=sqrt(1+h²), the derivative has the sign of 3cos²beta-H², hence one and only one interior maximizing height h_n=sqrt(3cos²beta-1). The two Taylor expansions as beta=pi/n tends to zero give n² p_n(h_n)->2pi²/(3sqrt3) and n⁴ p_n(sin beta)->pi⁴; the n=6 value and positivity checked separately. The n even restriction is essential for antipodal base vertex pairs. Random sections are central, not randomly offset or an affine-deformed Haar distribution.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified. Prior cubic and rectangular-box laws treat a base with four sides; Kovič (2013) classifies the regular-face polyhedron families without Haar section frequencies; Resultary mean-square width of regular prisms concerns a different observable. The exact n>=6 all-even maximal-section probability, unique height and two-scale asymptotics were not found in those actually inspected statements. Crucially, Voss (1982) publishes exact frequencies of n-polygons in planar polyhedron sections, and Ohser–Mücklich (1995) explicitly studies random regular-prism stereology. Their full texts could not be obtained from legitimate OA/arxiv searches and authorized institutional download reported VPN disconnected. Their abstracts suggest a different ensemble, random spatial affine-plane intersection rather than a Haar central plane; they remain significant priority risks. Inaccessibility alone does not mandate rejection, but no whole-document noncoverage judgment is made for either.
